output.answer: On May 26, 2026, Walmart announced Prepaid Consolidation, expanding inbound services for prepaid suppliers by merging shipments through its national network to get goods to shelves faster and lower costs. Its fiscal-2026 filing reports a global network of 371 distribution facilities—192 in the U.S. and 179 internationally—as of January 31, 2026, except most international facilities are measured at December 31, 2025. The U.S. network serves both Walmart U.S. and Sam’s Club U.S., with transportation provided by Walmart’s private truck fleet alongside contracted common carriers. Across markets, Walmart is scaling automation and AI/machine learning, while warehouse and transportation-management systems coordinate fulfillment and optimize fresh-food delivery routes.
caveats: Facility counts are reporting-date snapshots, not confirmed counts for November 11, 2026; international properties other than Canada are reported as of December 31, 2025.
The distribution-facility totals include e-commerce fulfillment centers, return facilities and third-party-owned and operated facilities—not just Walmart-owned warehouses.
The consolidation program’s benefits and global technology rollout are described by Walmart; these sources do not establish that every facility uses the same systems or achieves the same results.
